statement: Render the Stack bands in the desk's left rail over the pure model that already exists in src/lib/nav/stack-model.ts (stackModel, resumeBlock). FIRST, before writing any .tsx, call the design MCP tools ds_contract (intent: 'left rail stack bands: now, earlier today, queues, find'), ds_tokens (axis: spacing, then axis: typography) and ds_critique on src/components/sidebar/SidebarNavColumn.tsx — the PreToolUse hook refuses .tsx writes without that stamp, so do these calls first and again if a write is denied. Then create src/components/sidebar/RailStackBands.tsx: props { model: ReturnType<typeof stackModel>, onResume(id: string): void, onOpenQueue(tableId: string): void, onFind(): void }. It renders four labelled bands in the model's order — NOW (the armed block: title, state, elapsed as mm:ss), EARLIER TODAY (blocks newest-first, each a button that calls onResume), QUEUES (one button per queue that calls onOpenQueue), FIND (one button that calls onFind) — using the design-system Button and existing rail label styles; uppercase band labels; no new colours, no geometry animation, no tooltips. Mount it in src/components/sidebar/SidebarNavColumn.tsx directly below the pinned block and above the recents block, fed by stackModel over the current work sessions the column can already read; do not remove or reorder any existing nav leaf in this goal. Write src/components/sidebar/RailStackBands.test.ts using node:test with jsdom and React.createElement (no JSX) asserting the four band labels render in order and that clicking an earlier block calls onResume with its id. Touch no other file.
